production.note: US model years. First: Edmunds, 2006 M5 review: "The high-performance M5 returns to the BMW lineup for 2006, this time packing a 500-horsepower V10 engine." Last: Edmunds reviews the 2010 M5 (edmunds-2010-m5), and J.D. Power's M5 model-year list (a database) goes from 2010 to 2013 (the next generation), with no 2011 or 2012 (jdpower-m5-history). No opened page states in so many words that 2010 was the last E60 model year.

body.note: 'M5 Sedan'. The E61 M5 Touring was not sold in the US.

aspiration.note: 'the 5.0-liter V10 pumps out a maximum 500 hp at 7,750 rpm'; no forced induction.

drivetrain.note: Rear-wheel drive; no xDrive M5 in this generation.

transmission.note: "The standard transmission is the seven-speed sequential manual gearbox (SMG) ... A conventional six-speed manual transmission is a no-cost option." For 2006 Edmunds mentions only the SMG (edmunds-2006-m5). SMG is an automated manual.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Nominal output @ rpm hp 500 @ 7750 500 @ 7750 500 @ 7750" (M5 Sedan, M6 Coupe, M6 Convertible). Same rating for 2006: "500 horsepower at 7,750 rpm" (edmunds-2006-m5).

weightLb.note: Quote: "Weight M5 Sedan M6 Coupe M6 Convertible / Unladen lb 4012 3909 4398". BMW NA's 2009 US brochure gives one figure, not split by transmission (standard SMG; the 6-speed manual is a no-cost option). Reference year is 2009 because this is the earliest BMW NA weight that could be opened: the 2006 brochure (autocatalogarchive.com) returned 403 and the 2008 brochure returned 429.

sources.publisher: BMW of North America (brochure hosted by auto-brochures.com)
